howTo: Enter the catalogue dynamic load rating C and the equivalent dynamic bearing load P in the same load unit.
Choose ball or roller bearing, then enter the operating speed in rpm.
Use a1 only when its value is justified by the applicable reliability method; review L10 and adjusted Lna separately.
formula: L10 = (C / P)^p | L10h = (L10 x 10^6) / (60 x n) | Lna = a1 x L10 | p = 3 for ball bearings; p = 10/3 for roller bearings

examples.title: Ball bearing at a constant radial load
examples.description: An original screening example for a bearing with a 25 kN dynamic rating operating at 1,500 rpm.
notes: a1 = 1 leaves the basic L10 result unchanged and does not model contamination, lubrication, or mounting quality.
A short calculated life is a design signal, not a catalogue-selection decision by itself.

examples.title: Roller bearing with an adjusted reliability factor
examples.description: This comparison shows why bearing type and the selected adjustment factor must be documented.
notes: The a1 input is a multiplier in this screening tool. Establish its engineering basis outside the calculator.

references.title: ISO 281
references.note: Rolling bearing dynamic load ratings and rating life; use the current licensed edition for design decisions.

references.title: Bearing manufacturer catalogue
references.note: Use manufacturer-specific C values, operating limits, lubrication guidance, and application factors.

commonMistakes: Mixing C and P units, for example entering C in kN and P in N.
Using radial load alone when the bearing application requires an equivalent dynamic load calculation.
Treating L10 as a guaranteed service-life value or omitting the real load spectrum.
assumptions: The calculation assumes constant equivalent load and constant speed.
It uses the basic rating-life exponents for ball and roller bearings.
Lubrication, contamination, misalignment, temperature, installation, and transient load effects require separate engineering review.
